evidence.intree_statement: #[export] Program Instance multi_PreOrder `(R : crelation X) : PreOrder (multi R).
Theorem multi_R `(R : crelation X) (x y : X) : R x y → multi R x y.
Inductive multi `(R : crelation X) : crelation X := | multi_refl (x : X) : multi x x | multi_step (x y z : X) : R x y → multi y z → multi x z.

statement_record.book: Given a relation R on P, its reflexive-transitive closure is the free preorder on R: the minimally constrained preorder containing R, obtained by adding only the inequalities forced by reflexivity and transitivity; a graph (V,A,s,t) becomes a preorder by reading it as the relation {(s a, t a)} and closing. Minimality is explained as 'no further constraints on maps OUT of P', i.e. freeness is a left adjoint.
statement_record.intree: Inductive multi `(R : crelation X) : crelation X := multi_refl | multi_step ...; Theorem multi_R : R x y → multi R x y; Program Instance multi_PreOrder `(R : crelation X) : PreOrder (multi R).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the construction and the two positive clauses (it is a preorder; it contains R) are proved for an arbitrary relation, but the FREENESS clause — that it is the LEAST such preorder / the value of a left adjoint — is asserted only in the file's prose comment ('the least reflexive and transitive relation containing R'), never as a lemma. Also [multi] is Type-valued (crelation), so [multi R x y] is the type of R-paths rather than a truncated order relation: as stated it is the free CATEGORY on R-as-a-quiver with a PreOrder instance attached, not the quotient preorder the book builds. The graph-to-preorder passage (V,A,s,t) ↦ closure of {(s a, t a)} is nowhere in the tree, and there is no category of preorders/monotone maps in which to phrase the adjunction (Instance/Proset.v only turns one preorder into one thin category).

gap: Freeness/minimality is never stated: no lemma of the form 'if S is reflexive and transitive and R ⊆ S then multi R ⊆ S', no left-adjoint packaging, and no category of preorders and monotone maps to host it. Additionally multi is proof-relevant (paths), so the truncation that makes the closure a *preorder relation* rather than a free category is not performed, and the graph-to-relation-to-preorder route of the example is absent.

statement_record.book: For P a set, R ⊆ P×P, (P,≤_P) the reflexive-transitive closure, (Q,≤_Q) a preorder and f : P → Q an arbitrary function: (1) if R(x,y) implies f(x) ≤_Q f(y) then f is monotone (P,≤_P) → (Q,≤_Q); (2) conversely, if f is monotone then R(x,y) implies f(x) ≤_Q f(y). Together: the universal property of the free preorder.

statement_record.book: The free category Free(G) on a graph G has the vertices of G as objects and, as morphisms, the closure of the arrows of G under composition and identities — which turns out to be exactly the paths in G; Free(G) contains G and obeys no equations beyond those forced by the category axioms.

Program Definition ListMon : Category := {| obj := poly_unit; hom := fun _ _ => list bool; homset := fun _ _ => Morphism_equality _ _; id := fun _ => nil; compose := fun _ _ _ u v => (v ++ u)%list |}.  (header at :76-79: "The free monoid on [bool], as a one-object category: morphisms are lists of booleans, composition is concatenation"; Theorem funny_diagonals_distinct at :144 separates the words [true;false] and [false;true] in it) -- ADDED BY PHASE D, missed by Phase C; see verifier.notes

statement_record.book: Since monoids are one-object categories, for a set A let Loop(A) be the one-vertex graph with a loop for each a ∈ A; the free category on Loop(A) is a one-object category, hence a monoid — the free monoid on A. (1) the elements of the free monoid on {a}; (2) a well-known monoid isomorphic to it; (3) the elements of the free monoid on {a,b}.

verifier.notes: Classification PARTIAL confirmed (my blind pass reached PARTIAL too), but the record's evidence was INCOMPLETE and one of its claims is false. Verified evidence: Test/Issue138.v:95-96 really is `Example B138_free_loop_nodes : obj[FreeOnQuiver B138_loop] = Datatypes.unit := eq_refl.` with B138_loop defined at :87 as `Build_Quiver_Standard_Eq Datatypes.unit (fun _ _ => Datatypes.unit)` -- i.e. Loop({a}) -- quote and lines accurate. MISSED EVIDENCE (added by me to the evidence array): Construction/Funny/Comparison.v:81 defines `ListMon : Category` with obj := poly_unit, hom := fun _ _ => list bool, id := nil, compose := app -- a one-object category whose single hom-monoid is the free monoid on a TWO-element set, and its own header at :76-79 says so in as many words ('The free monoid on [bool], as a one-object category: morphisms are lists of booleans, composition is concatenation'). Theorem funny_diagonals_distinct (:144) then computes with two distinct elements of it, the words [true;false] and [false;true] -- exactly the content Exercise 5.24(3) asks for, on {a,b}. Consequently the strength_comparison's clause 'NOTHING in the tree performs the monoid identification' and the gap's '(a) no statement that a one-object category is a monoid' are overstated: a concrete free monoid IS realized in-tree as a one-object category, and its associativity/unit obligations are discharged by app_assoc/app_nil_r, which also contradicts the log line 'no monoid structure asserted for list A'. What genuinely remains missing, and keeps the item PARTIAL: no Loop(A) construction for general A; ListMon is built by hand rather than as FreeOnQuiver (Loop bool) and no isomorphism between the two is proved; no general delooping (one-object category -> Monoid object); no free-monoid left adjoint (Mon_Forget at Theory/Algebra/Monoid/Hom.v:93 confirmed to have no left adjoint anywhere); and parts (1)/(2) -- the free monoid on {a} and its iso to (ℕ,+,0) -- are entirely absent. Also verified the log's own citation of Construction/Cayley.v: the file exists and mentions 'the free monoid on a type' at :95 in prose only, so that line of the log is accurate.
